en: I praise the primordial Buddha of all Buddhas, whose nature is reality, who has expanded existence through the *tata* and *vitata* [sounds], whose essence is the sacrificial offering of the fortunate, who has performed manifold benefits, and who is the abode of splendors. *Sragdharāpañcakastotra* (The Fivefold Hymn in the Sragdharā Meter) by Śrī-Ārya-Nāgārjuna-pāda.
The embodiment of perfect enlightenment, manifesting the three qualities, the sole cause of the five wisdoms, formless and stainless, eternally pure like the sky—the shrine of the mind. (1)
Having merged into your own form of light through asceticism, and having crossed the ocean of generosity, ethical conduct, patience, vigor, meditation, and wisdom,
I have attained enlightenment within this most excellent of all cities, in the Akaniṣṭha realm, amidst the assembly of noble jewels.
I bow to you, whose form is the universe, appearing as manifold distinctions like a crystal gem.

Various medicines and excellent medicinal implements have been incessantly offered by all the people; what more shall I offer? Yet, with my mind intent on propitiating you, I have not yet renounced the wealth of my kingdom and other possessions.
And in birth after birth, I have accumulated a store of merit through body, speech, and mind— [The remainder of the verse would follow here.]
O one of excellent intellect, please accept all this, including my own body, which I shall offer to you. || 3 ||
The first is a pair, the third is a pair of pairs, then the fifth, the one known as the sixth,
the seventh and eighth, the one called the ninth, then the tenth, likewise the eleventh,
the one called the twelfth, the thirteenth, the fourteenth, and the "arrow-tortoise" (pañca-kūrma) produced all together from one source.
Thus, at that very moment, the entire world became your own infinite self; I bow to you, who are of one single form.
One is named Vairocana; another Jina is the Buddha known as Akṣobhya; that third is Ratnasambhava; the fourth in number is the one known as Amitābha (Amṛtaruc);
and the fifth is Amoghasiddhi—these being the well-known enumerations in the world.
I am forever bowed down before the gods, the Daityas, and mortals, who are all born from your own limbs. || 5 ||
The *Sragdharāpañcaka*, composed by the Buddha Śrīśākyasiṃha, is completed.
